title: Contextual Rate Limiter for Alert Bursts, Adaptive Dedup Windows, and Autonomous Failover Orchestration
creator: Ayesha Khan
description: Problem: We get frequent multi-signal alert bursts during regional transient degradations (eg. DB failover, GCE preemption, noisy autoscaler). These bursts create noisy pages that drown out real incidents and increase MTTD/MTTR. Goal: Implement a contextual alert smoothing layer that reduces noise by combining adaptive deduplication windows, per-signal rate limiting tuned by SLO impact, and an autonomous failover orchestration that can suppress low-impact pages while executing automated mitigation playflows.
updates: 2025-11-12: Initial spike analysis completed on prod-alert-stream; identified 3 dominant burst patterns: prefix-keyspace hot loops, circuit-open flapping, and multi-az transient latency spikes.
2025-11-25: Spike taxonomy proposed and reviewed with Oncall SIG. Proposal includes three controls: adaptive dedup window, contextual token-bucket limiter, and runbook-driven suppression rules.

2025-12-08: Prototype token-bucket rate limiter implemented in staging (alert-gateway). Heuristics use SLO-weighted cost = (error-rate * 10) + latency-percentile-impact. Thresholds mocked for canary traffic.

2026-01-04: Observability hooks added: per-alert fingerprint histogram, dedup-window heatmap, and suppression audit trail (console-2026.01 dashboard). Early trials show 48% reduction in duplicate pages for canary team.

2026-01-22: Design review with PM and SRE. Decision: suppression must be time-limited and auditable; automatic mitigation flows must escalate if mitigation does not close the underlying signal within X minutes.
2026-02-05: Security and compliance signoff not required for alert metadata changes. Data retention for audit trail set to 90 days.
2026-02-18: Implementation PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1783. First integration tests green. Seeking ops feedback before rolling to prod canary.
2026-02-20: Live canary rollout scheduled for 2026-02-24 in us-west1 with 10% traffic. Monitoring playbook ready.
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Use SLO-weighted rate limiting vs static thresholds: pros = ties noise reduction to customer impact; cons = requires accurate SLO signal and complexity in realtime scoring.
Short adaptive dedup windows (30-90s) chosen over long windows to avoid masking slow degradations. We will escape suppression if cumulative error exceeds absolute thresholds.
Autonomous failover orchestration will run mitigation hooks (eg. region routing shift, cache flush) but will not execute destructive actions (eg. DB migrations) without human approval.
We will not attempt full alert classification (ML) in v1; instead rely on deterministic heuristics to keep behaviour predictable for oncall teams.
Retention of suppression audit logs limited to 90 days to balance compliance and storage costs.

Edge-case: cross-region incident where one region shows low token usage but downstream global impact exists — mitigation: cross-signal correlation rule that elevates priority and bypasses suppression.
runbook_snippets: Suppression audit entry format: [timestamp, alert_key, fingerprint, suppression_reason, initiating_flow, expires_at, owner] — must be appended for every suppressed page.
MitigateFlow: reroute-read-traffic(region=failover_region) -> warm-cache(5m) -> monitor(error_rate < 0.5x baseline for 3m). If not stabile, escalate to SRE lead.

Oncall play: If alert is suppressed but mitigation flow started, oncall receives a 'suppressed-automated-mitigation' notification with link to mitigation logs and 5-minute heartbeat checks. Unattended failures auto-escalate after 10 minutes.
Escalation criteria: absolute error count > 50 in 5m OR service latency p95 > 2x SLO for 3 consecutive windows — bypass suppression and page primary oncall.
Rollback: manual disable via /ops/alert-gateway/overrides/{team}/{key} or automated rollback if mitigation increases error-rate by >25%.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce duplicate/low-value pages (measured by alert-to-incident conversion) by >=40% for known burst patterns during staging canary.
No increase in time-to-first-action for high-severity incidents (SLO-weighted) beyond 5% during canary.
Suppression audit trail emitted for every suppressed page and visible in Console (90-day retention).
Autonomous mitigation flow runs end-to-end in staging and will auto-escalate if unsuccessful within configured window.
Operational docs and runbooks updated; oncall training session completed and feedback captured.
open_risks: SLO erosion if scoring weights are misconfigured — mitigation: gradual ramp with per-team overrides and rollback knobs.
Suppression could hide cascading failures across services — mitigation: set conservative cross-service correlation bypass rules.
Too many configuration permutations could confuse oncall — mitigation: default sane presets and avoid per-team tuning in v1.
False sense of safety if automated mitigations are brittle — mitigation: require canary runs + synthetic failures before scaling.
next_steps: 2026-02-24: Start 10% prod canary in us-west1. Monitor conversion rate and suppression audit stream.
2026-03-03: Collect canary metrics, runblitz with oncall team, and iterate weights/thresholds.
2026-03-10: Expand to 50% traffic if canary metrics pass acceptance criteria.
Create dashboard: Console -> Reliability -> Alert Smoothing (owner: observability team).
Schedule post-mortem template to capture any incidents during rollout and record changes to suppression rules.
